Screen checkConfirm in Vanderbilt's Oracle or UKG during a recorded demo: who to contact when UKG access is missing; the label for turning down a time off request (Refuse or Reject); the Control Center and schedule screens managers use.

1 · Intro

When to use it.

Non-exempt (weekly and biweekly) pay depends on UKG time cards. The employee submits, the line manager approves, and payroll signs off before payroll runs. Run the weekly check so no one is paid late or wrong.

Your part as the HCM is to check, follow up, and step in when an employee can't enter their own time. Approving is the line manager's job.

Use this whenEvery week for your non-exempt employees, or when you need to enter hours or PTO for an employee who can't.

2 · Walk through

The weekly check, then editing time and entering PTO.

Check off each item as you read.

Approval State column
StateWhat it means for you
OpenNot submitted yet; follow up with the employee and line manager
SubmittedThe employee is done; the line manager still needs to approve
Approved (PayPrep Ready)Ready for payroll; no action needed

Before you approve

The same four checks on every pay-impacting transaction. Draft: the owner for this area confirms anything marked To confirm.

Attach

None. The approved time card is the record.

Check

  • Exceptions such as a missing punch are resolved before you approve.
  • You are in the completed pay period, not the open one.
  • Hours and pay codes match what the employee worked.
  • You did not submit this time card yourself. The person who submits a time card does not approve it.

To confirmPayroll to confirm the rule on who approves, and who approves when the manager is out.

Cutoff

Weekly and biweekly pay: time cards are due at noon on the Monday after the pay period ends, and holiday weeks move that. Check the HR/Payroll Calendar. After payroll signs off, an approval can't be removed unless payroll removes the sign-off first.

Who does what

  • Who starts it: The employee approves their own time card first.
  • Who approves: The manager approves. Payroll signs off.
  • What happens next: Payroll pays the approved hours.

Watch-outs

  • Empty time cards early in an open period are normal.
  • In an open period, Save. Don't Submit. Submitting means you must edit, update, and resubmit later.
  • One person does not both submit and approve the same time card. If you submit a time card for an employee, the manager approves it, not you.
  • Open item: Payroll to confirm the rule that the person who submits a time card does not approve it, and who approves when the manager is out.
  • Open item: add the UKG report that lists time cards not yet submitted, and how to schedule it.
  • Exempt employees' time off is managed in Oracle, not UKG.
  • Open item: confirm the label for turning down a time off request (Refuse or Reject).
  • Open item: document how a manager approves every line an employee submitted (select all, approve, then submit or approve again).
  • Open item: add how to add a schedule in UKG, and how to save a view that lists your student workers first.

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

  • UKG: Request Time Off from My Calendar (employees) (opens in a new tab)
  • UKG: Respond to time-off requests in Control Center (managers) (opens in a new tab)

HCM Academy quick guide · Payroll & Timecards

UKG time cards: the weekly check, edits, and time off

Use when: Every week for your non-exempt employees, or when you need to enter hours or PTO for an employee who can't. · System: UKG (Kronos)

  1. Open UKG from Oracle.
    • Don't see UKG on the Me tab? Select + under Apps; it may be one of the apps not shown.
  2. Open the current pay period for your employees.
    • Filter: in the row under the column headings, type your business unit under Business Unit (or your work unit under Work Unit), then select Refresh.
  3. Review each employee's punches.
  4. Compare the punches to the employee's schedule.
  5. Confirm every time card is complete and approved.
  6. Missing or late time card: contact the line manager.
  7. An error you can't resolve: contact payroll.
  8. Open UKG from Oracle.
    • Don't see UKG? Select + under Apps; it may be one of the apps not shown.
  9. Know the approval chain.
    • Employee submits
    • Line manager approves
    • Payroll signs off
  10. Open the time cards for your employees.
    • Filter: type your business unit under Business Unit (or your work unit under Work Unit), then select Refresh.
    • Tip: filter by Approval State to find time cards that should be submitted and aren't.
  11. Check each employee's status, hours, and exceptions.
  12. Submit for an employee who couldn't.
  13. Enter hours or PTO for an employee.
    • Then select Save at the top right. In an open period, Save only; don't Submit.
  14. Confirm the entry saved.
  15. Time off requests: check what's pending.
  16. Use schedules where they exist.
  17. Follow up until every time card is approved.
  18. Help employees with their own time cards.

  • Cutoff: Due at noon on the Monday after the pay period ends. Holiday weeks move it.

HCM Academy detailed job aid · Payroll & Timecards

Managing time cards and PTO in UKG

Step by step with screenshots. Screens from the HCM Academy training simulation of Oracle HCM. Names are fictional; check labels against Vanderbilt's Oracle.

  1. 01Open UKG from Oracle.

    On the Oracle Home page, on the Me tab, under Apps, select UKG (Kronos) Timesheets.

  2. 02Open the pay period list.

    On the UKG Home page, scroll down to Links and select By Pay Period. Timesheets (By Pay Period) opens on the most recently completed pay period.

  3. 03Filter to your employees.

    Use the filter row under the column headings. In this example, type the business unit under Business Unit, then select Refresh (the circular arrow at the right) to update the list.

  4. 04Choose the pay period.

    Use the arrows to the left and right of Pay Period to move between periods. The date range shows the period you're reviewing.

  5. 05Approve or edit time cards.

    Entering time is the employee's job. To act on a time card, check the box next to the employee's name, then choose Submit, Approve, or Reject at the top. To enter time for them (a system glitch, or a secondary time type such as PTO), open the time card, enter the time, and click Save. In an open pay period, don't Submit; you'd have to edit, update, and resubmit it later.

  6. 06Open the time card to enter PTO.

    With the box next to the employee's name checked, select View. Their time card opens in Timesheet Edit.

  7. 07Add a row on the day.

    Find the day and click + to add a row. The new row shows the employee's assignment.

  8. 08Enter the hours.

    Non-exempt PTO can be entered in 4-hour increments. Enter From and To, for example 8:00 am to 12:00 pm.

  9. 09Choose the PTO type.

    Raw Total shows 4.00. In the Time Off column, click Browse and pick the pay code, for example PTO-Vacation.

  10. 10Save. Don't Submit.

    Scroll up and click Save at the top right of Timesheet Edit. In an open pay period, leave it saved; don't Submit.
